P1.evidence: P1a N/A — no setter code in the title, no setter named, nothing to read back. P1b partial: the rep set three of the four parts, not four — 'I'm happy to walk you through the whole program, how it works, what's included, the investment side... But before I do that, I just want to get a quick picture of where you're actually at right now... what have you tried, and where you're trying to get to.' That covers where you are, where you want to go, and what you have tried; 'what you need' was never framed. P1c miss: the rep never asked for agreement; Andy volunteered 'Cool. Yeah, sounds good' unprompted, and the script credits asking. P1d hit: the frame itself functioned as the open invitation and Andy opened up at length off the back of it.

P2.evidence: P2a partial — height was asked directly ('And how tall you? 5\'7\"'), weight was volunteered ('I only weigh 64') and merely echoed back, and age was volunteered ('I'm 50') and never asked. P2b miss — the rep never asked what Andy does for work or whether it is desk-bound; the event-director and river-guiding history came out on its own. P2c partial — the rep asked one good follow-up, 'When did you do that surgery, the hip?', but never asked a general health-conditions or hereditary question; the twin brother's matching hips were volunteered. P2d partial — same reason: the hip replacements, arthritic shoulders, sore elbows and the four-week physio stint were all volunteered, with the rep only chasing duration on the hips. P2e hit — asked cleanly: 'And how many times a week do you work out?' P2f partial — 'Do you feel like there's anything, like, left on the table that could be more?' probes the outcome of current training, but the actual result that mattered ('made my shoulders better, and so I'm now surfing again') was volunteered rather than elicited. P2g hit — the rep pressed on diet twice and did not accept the first deflection: 'do you follow any kind of diet, or like, you eat all?' P2h and P2i miss — sleep and daily energy were never raised at all, which matters for a 50-year-old training eight to ten sessions a week.

P3.evidence: P3a hit — 'if you would have to say like in one sentence... what would be the like one thing that you want to work on?', which produced mobility. P3b partial — Andy named mobility himself; the rep never offered the strength/energy menu and instead used 'mobility, strength, that's one thing... second thing is nutrition' as a bridge into the pitch. P3c partial — the rep probed for a concrete physical target via the race ('you have this adventure race, so that's not your goal to be prepared for that?') but never asked the scripted 'something you want to do but can't right now'. P3d hit — the rep genuinely bridged outside the physical: 'In what way? You have a lot of time or what?', then 'To get back in the market, so to speak', then the strong one, 'Do you feel like you've lost that along the way?', which surfaced 'reconnecting to who I was and what I like doing.' P3e partial — the nearest move was 'what's the next level for you look like? Where do you want to get?', which is a goal question rather than a consequence-of-moving-better question. P3f partial — the rep supplied the answer rather than asking it: 'show your sons who's the man over here still.' P3g partial — identity and the marriage were live on the table and the rep dropped them, moving to training frequency instead of driving the thread; only the sons were touched, and only rhetorically. P3h hit — the reflect-back ran twice, 'wrapping it up, it sounds like, if I'm hearing correctly, like, you're doing good, basically. You're fit' and 'So basically you want to just learn how to progress with kettlebells, get stronger, show your sons who's the man over here still... That would be your main driver?', though it reflected a surface goal rather than the deeper identity driver the rep had already uncovered.

P4.evidence: The root-cause phase was effectively skipped, and that is why the close had no leverage. P4a partial — 'what have you tried' appeared once inside the opening frame and was never returned to. P4b and P4c miss — the rep never asked what happened with prior attempts or why they did not stick; Andy volunteered the most useful line in the call unprompted, 'I tried all these online programs, like fix your hips without surgery and stuff like that, and it didn't work,' and the rep did not pick it up. P4d and P4e miss — the obstacle question was never asked and Andy was never invited to name his own gap; he named it himself anyway ('I don't know enough about kettlebells'). P4f partial — the rep did run a real DIY challenge, 'But you could double down. Like if you have so much experience and your son is also studying similar things, you could put it on your own. You could set it up, the whole program,' but it tested competence rather than consistency, and when Andy answered 'Yeah, I could,' the rep let it go instead of pressing.

P5.evidence: Entirely absent. No version of 'if nothing changes, what does life look like over the next two years' was asked, no settling question, no 'why not', no line in the sand. This is the largest single gap in the call. The rep had two ready-made consequence levers handed to him — an artificial hip that 'can pop out more easily' and joints that already ache from traditional lifting at 50 — and used neither. Instead he actively removed the consequence: 'From what I'm hearing, it's not something that's wrong right now, you're just basically trying to, I don't know, optimize a little bit better,' and later 'you're not our typical client because you're way ahead.' Having told the prospect nothing is wrong, there was no cost of inaction left to sell against.

P6.evidence: P6a miss — the belief question was never asked in any form. P6b partial and badly out of sequence — the rep did ask 'So apart from finances, like, sounds good to you, like there's nothing else?', which is the right shape, but he asked it after the price rather than before presenting, so it functioned as objection isolation rather than as a commitment check. P6c miss — the whole point of the phase is a clear yes before anything is presented, and the rep went from discovery straight into the three pillars, the delivery mechanics and a dollar figure without ever securing one. When hesitation surfaced he did not return to Phase 5, he booked Friday. The only post-presentation temperature check, 'So how do you actually feel about it? Because does this meet your needs?', is a needs question, not a commitment question, and Andy's answer ('Yeah, I think it would meet my needs') was immediately qualified into a shorter engagement.

P11.evidence: A price was quoted and the rep described the sequence in the abstract — 'we settled the payments, I get you on the onboarding call with Trevor, and you can start whenever you want' — but no verbal yes was obtained, so none of the four steps became reachable on this call. Scored N/A rather than miss so the phase does not double-penalise the P6 failure that caused it.

objection_plays.detail: Ran the first move well and then abandoned the play. ISOLATE FIRST was executed properly — 'So apart from finances, like, sounds good to you, like there's nothing else?' — and it produced a clean isolation: 'no, apart from the finances... Everything else, the way that it works and what I think I would get out of it are good.' From there nothing else ran. No 'you're not in a SHOULD I place, you're in a HOW place'. No payment-plan door opened, despite it being the obvious unlock for a prospect who converts USD into NZD and calls it a substantial portion of annual income — 'most clients pay upfront, but for some we break it up' was never said, and the offer stayed a single upfront payment. No permission asked for an open financial conversation. Not one of the six financial-picture questions was asked: cash on hand, monthly surplus after bills, number of credit cards, available credit per card, used versus available, or crypto/stocks/investments. The rep substituted a logistics question — 'what's the timeline on figuring out with the New Zealand feel, like, how to run it through the...' — and then booked a follow-up.

The trigger was explicit — 'So I will, let me think, and I can have some time to think about that, right?' — and the play did not run at all. The rep answered 'Let me know what are your thoughts on that' and moved to scheduling. None of the seven moves were attempted: no 'do you feel what we've gone through CAN get you to your goal', no 'what makes you feel it can', no 'so what's actually coming up that's preventing you from getting started', no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', no 'when do you make a different decision', no 'that man you want to be, how does HE decide right now', and no final 'are you sure, nothing else keeping you from being 100% in'. Granting the delay unchallenged converted a live call into a follow-up.

SCRIPT GAP, not a rep failure — a tax-deductibility and foreign-currency objection with no scripted play. Andy's first stated blocker was 'I have to figure out if I can run it through my business, for one,' and he laid out the arithmetic himself: 'the $4,000 US dollars becomes about $2,800 US dollars if I run the business.' He then added a second, larger currency problem: 'that's really looking at about 7,500 New Zealand dollars for me because of the exchange rate.' The playbook has nothing for either. Objection C assumes the blocker is capacity to pay, so it offers no path for a prospect who can pay but is trying to make the purchase tax-efficient, and no path for a non-US prospect whose real price is inflated ~87% by FX. The rep improvised a clarifying question and then deferred. Worth building a play here: this prospect had explicitly floated becoming a trainer, which is the professional-development case his accountant needs, and nobody helped him make it.

SECOND SCRIPT GAP — a free alternative, supplied by Primal itself, that genuinely worked. Andy is anchored on Trevor's free content and the downloadable Guide, and reported a real clinical result from them: 'one of the things I started doing of Trevor's that I really liked was the halo workout, he calls it 28s... made my shoulders better, and so I'm now surfing again, and without as much pain.' He then argued the general case against paying for structure: 'really it all works... what it takes is consistency, you have to show up consistently... it's not like the kettlebell's a magical tool.' This is the same shape as the known '$29/mo coach' gap, but harder, because the substitute is the company's own marketing. No play exists and none was improvised; the rep agreed with the framing rather than contesting it.

notes: Strong rapport and genuinely good diet questioning, undone by skipping the two phases that create urgency: root cause (P4) and the consequence frame (P5) were essentially not run, and no commitment was taken before presenting (P6). The rep then compounded it by removing his own leverage — telling a man with two artificial hips and arthritic shoulders that 'it's not something that's wrong right now' and that he is 'way ahead' of the typical client — and by down-selling to a three-month tier unprompted, before price was on the table, which still did not save the deal. Coach two things for Friday: build the cost-of-inaction case around the hip dislocation risk and the joint damage from traditional lifting, and run Objection C properly, starting with the payment-plan door that was never opened. Also flag for review: the $4,000 / 3-month tier is not in the documented offer, and at 00:09:07 the rep asked the prospect for medical advice about his own hip, inverting the frame for roughly three minutes.
